topic: understanding the concept of like terms in algebra

easy.text: Which of the following is a 'like term' to 3x?

options.feedback: Correct -- both terms have the same variable (x) raised to the same power (1), making them like terms.
This has a different exponent (x² vs x), so it isn't a like term to 3x.
This has a different variable (y instead of x), so it isn't a like term to 3x.
This is a constant with no variable at all, so it isn't a like term to 3x.

medium.text: In the expression 5x + 3y - 2x + 7y, which terms can be combined together?

options.feedback: Correct -- only terms with matching variables can be combined: the x-terms together, and the y-terms together.
These have different variables (x and y), so they cannot be combined as like terms.

options.text: All four terms can be combined into one single term
options.feedback: Only terms sharing the same variable can be combined -- x-terms and y-terms must be kept separate.

options.text: None of the terms can be combined
options.feedback: There are matching like terms present here (the two x-terms and the two y-terms) that can indeed be combined.
Correct -- combine the x² terms (4x²-2x²=2x²) and the xy terms (3xy+5xy=8xy) separately, leaving the y² term alone since nothing else matches it.
This has the wrong sign on the y² term.
This incorrectly adds the two x² terms instead of subtracting.
This incorrectly drops the exponent on the combined x² term.

easy.hard: Only terms that share both the same variable AND the same exponent can be considered alike.
easy.medium: Look for a term with the exact same variable and power.
easy.easy: Look for another term with just an x, like 3x has.

medium.hard: Group each term by its specific variable before combining, keeping different variables entirely separate.
medium.medium: Group the x-terms together and the y-terms together separately.
medium.easy: Add the two x-terms together, and separately add the two y-terms together.

hard.hard: Only combine terms that match in both variable type AND exponent -- treat x², xy, and y² as three entirely distinct term categories.
hard.medium: Combine the x² terms together, combine the xy terms together, and leave the y² term as is since nothing else matches it.
hard.easy: Combine the x² terms, combine the xy terms, and leave the y² term alone.
